response.sql: WITH grp AS (SELECT t.telescregistry AS telescope, o.weathprofile AS weathprofile, AVG(s.modindex) AS avg_mod, AVG(s.phaseshiftdeg) AS avg_phase FROM signals s JOIN telescopes t ON t.telescregistry = s.telescref JOIN observatories o ON o.observstation = t.observstation GROUP BY t.telescregistry, o.weathprofile), base AS (SELECT AVG(avg_mod) AS baseline FROM grp), kept AS (SELECT g.weathprofile, g.avg_mod, g.avg_phase, g.avg_mod - b.baseline AS excess FROM grp g CROSS JOIN base b WHERE g.avg_mod > b.baseline) SELECT weathprofile, AVG(avg_mod) AS avg_modulation_index, AVG(avg_phase) AS avg_phase_shift, AVG(excess) AS avg_excess_over_baseline FROM kept GROUP BY weathprofile;

assumptions.assumption: Inner joins from signals to telescopes to observatories drop signals with no matching telescope or observatory.
The baseline is one global mean of all telescope/weather group averages, with each group counting equally. It is not computed separately for each weather profile.
AVG ignores NULL modulation index and phase shift values. Groups whose average modulation index is NULL cannot exceed the baseline, so they are dropped.
